lessons.text: Never use appeal to ignorance (Treating the absence of disproof as proof (or the reverse)). It cost you against William James Sidis.

Prepare an answer before you assert: William James Sidis broke through with "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. When the measured results are compared across studies, then the pattern i…" (Clean argument. structure=1.00, evidence=0.50).

Prepare an answer before you assert: William James Sidis broke through with "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the premise survives test…" (Clean argument. structure=0.50, evidence=1.00).

Borrow this pattern from William James Sidis: "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the premise survives test…" — it answered the opponent directly, it carried evidence, its premises led cleanly to the conclusion.

Your weakest move against William James Sidis was "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. Because a four-day week costs more than it returns, the documented cases…" (soundness 0.20). State its premises and evidence before you use it again.
